title: Sell Mineral Rights in Mount Vernon, AL

metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Mount Vernon, AL | Mobile County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Mount Vernon, AL in north Mobile County? Get a courthouse-checked, no-pressure offer close to the Citronelle field.
heroLead: Mount Vernon sits in north Mobile County within reach of the Citronelle trend, on ground with a longer federal and family land history than most of its neighbors, going back to the old Mount Vernon Arsenal tract.
intro: The federal reservation that once surrounded the arsenal at Mount Vernon shaped how the surrounding private land was surveyed and sold off over the following century, and a good bit of the rural acreage nearby has stayed in the same families since. When the Citronelle Field's leasing activity pushed outward from its core in the mid-twentieth century, some of that older Mount Vernon-area land got picked up in the process, while other tracts nearby were never leased at all.

sections.heading: Old Federal Land, Later Private Hands
paragraphs: If your family's land near Mount Vernon traces back to a federal land sale or an early homestead, that history can actually make title easier to confirm, since federal patents are well documented. We check that chain first before looking at what leasing activity, if any, followed.

sections.heading: How Close Is Close Enough to Citronelle?
paragraphs: Being near a major field doesn't automatically mean your tract has been leased or drilled — proximity helps, but it isn't proof. We check the actual lease and drilling record for your specific parcel before saying whether it's producing, held for future development, or simply undeveloped acreage on the edge of an active area.

faqs.question: Our land traces back to an old federal land patent. Does that complicate things?
faqs.answer: Usually the opposite — federal patents are well documented, which makes the early part of the title chain easier to confirm.

faqs.question: We're close to Citronelle but have never been approached about leasing. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, proximity to a field doesn't guarantee leasing activity on every nearby tract. We check your specific parcel's actual history.

faqs.question: How do you value land that's never produced but sits near an active field?
faqs.answer: As undeveloped acreage, priced against nearby activity rather than as a producing interest. It's a different, generally lower starting point, but not zero.

faqs.question: Does the old arsenal history affect our mineral title at all today?
faqs.answer: Not directly for most private tracts nearby, but we still check whether any portion of your family's land traces back through the original federal survey.

faqs.question: Who do we talk to first if we're not sure what we own?
faqs.answer: Send us whatever documentation you have and we'll do the courthouse research ourselves before you have to make any decision.
